section: Profiling metabolites from cultured CCLE cell lines
text: Li et al. profiled 225 metabolites in 928 cancer cell lines by targeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS). The panel included 124 polar and 101 lipid species.

The LC-MS peak areas are relative signals. Signals for the same metabolite can be compared across cell lines after normalization. Raw signal intensities cannot be used to compare abundances of different metabolites or to infer absolute concentrations or metabolic flux.

Pooled lysates provided a reference for scaling signals across batches. For each analyte, each sample was normalized against the nearest pooled reference and then corrected for batch offsets. The supplement includes standardized peak areas and a separate transformed analysis matrix.
The paper found that tissue lineage explained more than 10% of the variation for 148 of the 225 profiled metabolites. It includes lineage covariates in cross-lineage association analyses.

Version 4 of DepMap Public 20Q2 changed the gene-expression file from TSV to CSV and updated RNA sequencing data for three cell lines. ACH-prefixed DepMap identifiers link expression, mutation calls, and cell-line metadata.

CCLE expression describes RNA transcript abundance in log2(TPM+1) units. The gene-column labels include the gene symbol and NCBI Entrez Gene identifier. Expression does not directly measure protein abundance or enzyme activity.

The illustrative pathway treats lactate as a single pool with constant supply and first-order clearance. Supply and clearance parameters are assumptions. The simulator is not linked to a cell line, calibrated to longitudinal measurements, or validated as a digital twin.

Tissue lineages are held out as groups. Feature imputation, scaling, and ridge regularization selection occur within training data. An unseen lineage falls back to the training median for the lineage-only baseline. Evaluation is internal to CCLE and reports prediction error, not a causal relationship.
